```ts
    expect((err as A0RecoveryError).code).toBe('E_A0_RECOVERY_DUPLICATE_NULLIFIER');
    expect(fake.liveHandle()).toBeNull();
    expect(mmkvSecure()!.getString(KEY)).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('control: with nothing of ours spent, the change step reads no nullifier and the restore succeeds', async () => {
    const chain = fresh();
    ownDeposit(chain, 0n, 1_000_000n);
    appendWithdraw(chain, {nullifier: strangerField(5), changeCommitment: strangerField(6)});
    appendWithdraw(chain, {nullifier: strangerField(5), changeCommitment: strangerField(7)});
    expect((await restore(chain)).notes.map(n => n.status)).toEqual(['unspent']);
  });
});

describe('the restore into an existing store (chain truth wins for note state)', () => {
  it('a stored note mid-unshield (pending, pendingSince) whose spend LANDED becomes spent with the landed tx; its change comes back', async () => {
    const chain = fresh();
    const d0 = ownDeposit(chain, 0n, 1_000_000n);
    addA0PendingDeposit({commitment: d0.commitment, amount: 1_000_000n, rho: d0.rho, depositIndex: 0n, lastValidBlockHeight: 1});
    confirmA0Deposit(d0.rho, {leafIndex: d0.leafIndex, commitment: d0.commitment});
    // what Task 7 writes before submit: the note pending with pendingSince (chain time)
    mmkvSecure()!.set(
      KEY,
      mmkvSecure()!.getString(KEY)!.replace('"status":"unspent"', '"status":"pending","pendingSince":1763400000'),
    );
    expect(loadA0NoteStore().notes[0]).toMatchObject({status: 'pending', pendingSince: 1763400000});
    const u = ownUnshield(chain, d0, {to: STRANGER});
    await restore(chain);
    expect(loadA0NoteStore().notes).toEqual([
      {commitment: d0.commitment, amount: 1_000_000n, rho: d0.rho, depositIndex: 0n, leafIndex: 17, status: 'spent', spentTx: u.signature},
      {commitment: u.commitment, amount: 590_000n, rho: u.rho, leafIndex: 18, status: 'unspent'},
    ]);
  });

  it('a stored spent note WITHOUT spentTx (an M1b restore) gets it; a stored spent note is never made unspent', async () => {
    const chain = fresh();
    const d0 = ownDeposit(chain, 0n, 1_000_000n);
    const d1 = ownDeposit(chain, 1n, 2_000_000n);
    const u = ownUnshield(chain, d0, {to: STRANGER});
    mergeA0RecoveredNotes(
      [
        {commitment: d0.commitment, amount: 1_000_000n, rho: d0.rho, depositIndex: 0n, leafIndex: 17, status: 'spent'},
        {commitment: d1.commitment, amount: 2_000_000n, rho: d1.rho, depositIndex: 1n, leafIndex: 18, status: 'spent'},
      ],
      2n,
    );
    await restore(chain);
    const notes = loadA0NoteStore().notes;
    expect(notes[0]).toEqual({commitment: d0.commitment, amount: 1_000_000n, rho: d0.rho, depositIndex: 0n, leafIndex: 17, status: 'spent', spentTx: u.signature});
    expect(notes[1]).toEqual({commitment: d1.commitment, amount: 2_000_000n, rho: d1.rho, depositIndex: 1n, leafIndex: 18, status: 'spent'});
  });
});

  });

      const u2 = ownUnshield(chain, {rho: u1.rho, amount: u1.amount}, {to: to(far)});

    const r23 = await run(23);
    expect(r23.exitAccounts).toEqual(['slip10:3', 'slip10:23']);

    expect(registry()).toEqual([['slip10:0', 'main', acct(0).address]]);
    expect(res.stats.exitAccounts).toBe(1); // matched (index 0), already the main
  });

    expect(registry()).toEqual([

    expect(res.stats.accountIndicesTried).toBe(20);
  });

    storeTransparentScheme({kind: 'cli'});
    const chain = fresh();
    const d0 = ownDeposit(chain, 0n, 1_000_000n);

    const res = await restore(chain);
    expect(res.exitAccounts).toEqual([]);

    expect(loadA0AccountRegistry()!.map(e => [e.scheme, e.role])).toEqual([['cli', 'main']]);

    expect(reserved.scheme).toBe('slip10:1');
    const chain = fresh();
    const d0 = ownDeposit(chain, 0n, 1_000_000n);
    ownUnshield(chain, d0, {to: to(1)});
    const res = await restore(chain);

    expect(registry()).toEqual([
      ['slip10:0', 'main', acct(0).address],
      ['slip10:1', 'fresh-exit', acct(1).address],
    ]);
  });

  it('WRITE ORDER: an unreadable registry refuses the restore BEFORE the notes are written (the next start restores again)', async () => {
    mmkvSecure()!.set('v1_accounts', '{"schema":1,"accounts":[]}');
    const chain = fresh();
    const d0 = ownDeposit(chain, 0n, 1_000_000n);
    ownUnshield(chain, d0, {to: to(1)});
    await expect(restore(chain)).rejects.toMatchObject({code: 'E_A0_ACCOUNTS_CORRUPT'});
    expect(mmkvSecure()!.getString(KEY)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(fake.liveHandle()).toBeNull();
  });

  it('the seed is zero-filled after the account walk used it; keysOpen got a copy (also zero-filled)', async () => {
    const chain = fresh();
    const d0 = ownDeposit(chain, 0n, 1_000_000n);
    ownUnshield(chain, d0, {to: to(1)});
    const seed = seedBytes(TEST_SEED);
    const res = await restore(chain, seed);
    expect(res.exitAccounts).toEqual(['slip10:1']); // the walk had the seed after keysOpen consumed its copy
    expect(seed.every(b => b === 0)).toBe(true);
    expect(callsOf('keysOpen')).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```

```diff
+/** `matchSpent`'s answer held to its contract: integers, ascending, each < `count`. */
+function checkedIndices(answer: number[], count: number): number[] {
+  let prev = -1;
+  for (const k of answer) {
+    if (!Number.isInteger(k) || k <= prev || k >= count) {
+      throw new A0RecoveryError('E_A0_RECOVERY_NATIVE', `matchSpent answered ${JSON.stringify(answer)} for ${count} notes`);
+    }
+    prev = k;
+  }
+  return answer;

+/**

+ * with index 0; the program side's golden step `rho_change`). The input is a PUBLIC nullifier —
+ * one that is on chain already — never an unspent note's (R12). 64 lowercase BE hex in and out.
+ */
+export function a0ChangeRho(nullifierHex: string): string {
+  return toBe32Hex(rhoOut(BigInt(`0x${nullifierHex}`), 0));
+}
+
+/** `changeAmount = inputAmount − withdrawAmount − fee` (§3), or null when the spend exceeds the input. */
+export function a0ChangeAmount(inputAmount: bigint, withdrawAmount: bigint, fee: bigint): bigint | null {
+  const change = inputAmount - withdrawAmount - fee;
+  return change < 0n ? null : change;

+  unmatchedChangeLeaves: number;

+interface Spender {

+ * `matchSpent`); they are copied, not changed.

+export async function recoverA0ChangeNotes(
+  handle: A0Handle,

+  /** indices into `notes` of spent notes not yet attributed to a nullifier */
+  let waiting = notes.flatMap((n, k) => (n.status === 'spent' ? [k] : []));
+  if (waiting.length === 0) {
+    // nothing of ours is spent: no change note can exist, and no matchSpent is made
+    return {notes, changeNotes: 0, unmatchedChangeLeaves: 0, exitDestinations: [], attributionCalls: 0};
+  }
+  const spenders = new Map<string, Spender>();
+  for (const tx of tree.txs) {
+    for (const n of tx.withdrawNullifiers) {
+      if (spenders.has(n)) {
+        throw new A0RecoveryError(
+          'E_A0_RECOVERY_DUPLICATE_NULLIFIER',
+          `nullifier ${n} is spent by ${spenders.get(n)!.tx.signature} and ${tx.signature}`,
+        );
+      }
+      spenders.set(n, {tx, withdrawal: tx.withdrawals.find(w => w.nullifier === n) ?? null});
+    }
+  }
+  const allNullifiers = [...spenders.keys()];
+  const open = [...allNullifiers];
+  const destinations: string[] = [];
+  let changeNotes = 0;
+  let unmatchedChangeLeaves = 0;
+  let attributionCalls = 0;
+
+  while (waiting.length > 0) {
+    const found: A0Note[] = [];
+    let attributed = 0;
+    for (const n of [...open]) {
+      if (waiting.length === 0) {
+        break;
+      }
+      attributionCalls++;
+      const answer = checkedIndices(
+        await a0MatchSpent(
+          handle,
+          [n],
+          waiting.map(k => notes[k]!.rho),

+      if (answer.length === 0) {
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (answer.length > 1) {

+      }
+      const k = waiting[answer[0]!]!;
+      waiting = waiting.filter(j => j !== k);
+      open.splice(open.indexOf(n), 1);
+      attributed++;
+      const {tx, withdrawal: w} = spenders.get(n)!;
+      const note = notes[k]!;
+      note.spentTx = tx.signature;
+      if (w === null) {
+        unmatchedChangeLeaves++; // a Withdraw event without its instruction: spent, no change to read
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (!destinations.includes(w.destination)) {
+        destinations.push(w.destination);
+      }
+      const changeAmount = a0ChangeAmount(note.amount, w.amount, w.fee);
+      if (changeAmount === null) {
+        unmatchedChangeLeaves++;
+        continue;
+      }
+      const rho = a0ChangeRho(n);
+      const commitment = await a0Commitment(handle, changeAmount, rho);
+      if (commitment !== w.changeCommitment) {
+        unmatchedChangeLeaves++;
+        continue;
+      }
+      const leaves = tx.leafInserted.filter(l => l.commitment === commitment);
+      if (leaves.length !== 1) {
+        throw new A0RecoveryError(
+          'E_A0_RECOVERY_LEAF',
+          `${tx.signature}: ${leaves.length} LeafInserted of the change commitment ${commitment}`,
+        );
+      }
+      found.push({commitment, amount: changeAmount, rho, leafIndex: leaves[0]!.leafIndex, status: 'unspent'});
+    }
+    if (attributed === 0) {
+      throw new A0RecoveryError(
+        'E_A0_RECOVERY_NATIVE',
+        `${waiting.length} notes are spent and no synced nullifier spends them`,
+      );
+    }
+    if (found.length > 0) {
+      const base = notes.length;
+      notes.push(...found);
+      changeNotes += found.length;
+      const spent = checkedIndices(
+        await a0MatchSpent(
+          handle,
+          allNullifiers,
+          found.map(f => f.rho),
+        ),
+        found.length,
+      );
+      for (const j of spent) {
+        notes[base + j]!.status = 'spent';

+export interface A0ExitAccountRecovery {
+  /** the `slip10` indices whose ATA is an exit destination, ascending */
+  indices: number[];
+  /** indices derived */
+  tried: number;

+/**
+ * §7 "Accounts" (I6): which `slip10:n` of `seed` own the exit `destinations` — `ATA(slip10:n,
+ * mint)` for n = 0, 1, …, stopping `A0_ACCOUNT_DISCOVERY_GAP` indices past the highest match (or
+ * when every destination is matched). Local only; writes nothing. A `cli` wallet has no exit
+ * accounts (S9): nothing is derived. `seed` is borrowed (not wiped here).
+ */
+export function recoverA0ExitAccountIndices(seed: Uint8Array, destinations: readonly string[]): A0ExitAccountRecovery {
+  if (loadTransparentScheme().kind === 'cli' || destinations.length === 0) {
+    return {indices: [], tried: 0};
+  }
+  const want = new Set(destinations);
+  const indices: number[] = [];
+  let highest = -1;
+  let n = 0;
+  for (; n <= highest + A0_ACCOUNT_DISCOVERY_GAP && n <= A0_MAX_ACCOUNT_INDEX && indices.length < want.size; n++) {
+    const owner = new PublicKey(a0AccountAddress(seed, {kind: 'slip10', account: n}));
+    if (want.has(a0AtaOf(owner).toBase58())) {
+      indices.push(n);
+      highest = n;
+    }
+  }
+  return {indices, tried: n};
+}
```

#### Notes for the executor (Task 5)

- **The rulings this task took (each the most secure default; the owner may overturn any):**
  - **The attribution, as built.** In sync order, one `matchSpent(handle, [n], <the spent notes not yet attributed>)` per
    synced `Withdraw` nullifier, stopping as soon as every spent note is attributed; each new round (change notes found
    spent) re-asks only the nullifiers not yet attributed. Every call is local (no request), so the order and the count
    reveal nothing. The bound: at most (synced nullifiers) calls per round and at most (synced nullifiers) rounds. On
    devnet today that is a few dozen JNI calls per restore, each a Poseidon per own rho. A round that attributes nothing
    while notes wait refuses (`E_A0_RECOVERY_NATIVE`). Without that guard the loop would spin forever on a core that
    contradicts itself (mutation C10). The row that holds it bounds its own spy (it throws after 200 single-nullifier
    calls): an unbounded loop of resolved promises starves Jest's timers, so without the bound the mutant hung the run
    until the 600 s wall limit (first round). Cost if wrong: a restore refuses instead of hanging.
  - **A change leaf that is not ours is counted, not thrown** (`unmatchedChangeLeaves`). Only a holder of `nk` can spend
    our note, but the circuit takes `change_d` as a free private input, so another implementation holding our `nk` could
    leave the change under another diversifier. Our wallet never does that (R9: every own note is under `d_self`). The
    note is still `spent` with its `spentTx`; nothing is imported. Two other cases are counted the same way: a `Withdraw`
    event without its instruction (the sync cannot produce one today) and a spend above the note's amount (the circuit
    forbids one). Throwing in any of these would block the restore of every note of the wallet. Cost if wrong: such a
    change, if it were ours, stays unrecovered and the counter shows it.
  - **The duplicate-nullifier refusal is read only when a note of ours is spent.** `E_A0_RECOVERY_DUPLICATE_NULLIFIER`
    mirrors M1b's `E_A0_RECOVERY_DUPLICATE_RHO` (the nullifier PDA is `init`: the chain cannot hold two). Unlike the rho
    one, a wallet with nothing spent never reads it, so an impossible pool-wide anomaly cannot block a wallet that is
    not involved (row + control).
  - **A zero change is imported** (amount 0, `unspent`). The program side's `zero_change` vector says it is still a
    leaf, and Task 7's settle path must store it the same way, so a restore and a settle agree. It is never a source:
    "the largest unspent note" of §6 cannot be a 0-amount note while any other exists.
  - **Exit destinations come from every withdrawal that spent one of OUR notes**, its change ours or not: only `nk`
    spends our note, so the exit is ours either way. A stranger's withdrawal to an address of our seed is not an exit of
    ours, and the restore does not add it (row).
  - **The account walk stops early once every destination matched** — the result is the rule's (no later index can
    match one more), with fewer derivations. A match on the MAIN (an unshield to "My main account") is a match: it moves
    the 20-index window but changes no role. `cli` wallets and restores with no exit destination derive nothing.
  - **Write order: the registry first, then the notes.** The note record's absence makes the next start restore again
    (`startup.ts`). So a registry that refuses — an unreadable record (`E_A0_ACCOUNTS_CORRUPT`) or a main that is not
    the wallet's scheme (`E_A0_ACCOUNTS_MAIN`) — refuses the whole restore with nothing written. The restore never
    replaces a corrupt registry: Task 2's rule is "never helpful", and this task does not add a replace path. Cost if
    wrong: a wallet whose registry is unreadable shows the startup error until that is resolved, instead of a balance
    with exit accounts silently missing.
  - **The seed.** `keysOpen` consumes (zero-fills) what it is given, and the account walk needs the seed after the handle
    is closed. The restore therefore hands `keysOpen` a copy (`seed.slice()`) and zero-fills the copy and the caller's
    seed in its `finally` (mutation A6). The keys are live only while matching, as before. The seed is in JS memory
    during the walk (20–40 SLIP-0010 derivations), which is no change from what `a0SeedPublicKeys` already does there.
  - **Chain truth for note state.** M1b's merge kept a stored `spent` note as it was. Now a recovered spend that names
    its tx replaces it, so `spentTx` is filled for an M1b-restored note and corrected if it differed. A recovered spend
    WITHOUT `spentTx` — the deposit pre-check's import, which runs no attribution — never replaces a stored `spent` note,
    and nothing turns a `spent` note back (row). This follows the controller's FYI ruling: a landed tx's nullifier is spent.
  - **`@scure/base`: declared, not replaced.** `depositFlow.ts` uses it for the mint's bytes and the deposit signature's
    base58 encoding, and five other files of the app import it undeclared as well: `src/utils/isOnCurveAddress.ts`,
    `src/modules/presale/referralInput.ts`, `core/presale/referrer.ts`, `core/solana/{rpc,broadcast}.ts`, plus the
    desk and vector scripts. Switching `depositFlow.ts` alone would fix one of six. The package resolved to 2.0.0 already (a
    dependency of `@scure/bip32` / `@scure/bip39`), so the declaration `^2.0.0` changes nothing installed. The lockfile
    diff is one line (the root's `dependencies`), written by `npm install --package-lock-only --offline --ignore-scripts`
    under npm 11.6.2 (the CI pin).
- **The golden (R6′) and the naming.** The program side's file names the steps of one `withdraw_change`. Reconciled
  with our §3:
  - `nullifier_in = Poseidon3(0x11, nk, rho_in)` is our `nullifier(rho)` of the note being spent (public input [1]).
  - `rho_change = Poseidon3(0x13, nullifier_in, 0)` is our `rho_change`: `fieldEquations.ts` `rhoOut(n, 0)`, recovery's
    `a0ChangeRho`, Rust's `rho_change`.
  - `addrField_self = Poseidon3(0x12, nk, change_d)` is our `addrField(d)` with `d = change_d`.
  - `changeCommitment = Poseidon5(0x10, addrField_self, changeAmount, mintHash, rho_change)` is our
    `commitment(changeAmount, rho_change)`.
  - **The difference is only in the diversifier.** Their vectors use `change_d = 987654321 ≠ d_in = 123456789`: the
    circuit takes `change_d` as its own private input. Our wallet fixes `d = change_d = d_self` for every own note (R9,
    §3 `prove`: "`d = change_d = d_self`"). So their `addrField_self` is our `addrField(d_self)` only when `change_d = d_self`,
    which is always the case for a note of ours.
  - **What the golden proves here:** the composition — j = 0, the instruction's amount AND fee, the argument order, the
    tags — through our JS equations and our recovery helpers, with the three rejected variants as negative controls.
  - **What it cannot prove here:** Rust's own composition. `keysOpen` takes a seed, not an `nk`. Rust is held to
    `a0-key-vectors.json` (`rhoChange` and `commitment` rows, 25 notes; written by `fieldEquations.ts`, which this
    golden now holds). The change commitment Rust computes inside `prove` is checked on the chain by every landed
    unshield (§6.8, Task 4) and at the checkpoint (Task 9).
  - **§15's open point "a golden `changeCommitment` row with its inputs" is closed by 2146368.** The controller's
    ruling 6 ("proceed with the composition") is superseded: the row exists and is compared.
- **S15's reach, as built.** The constant has one home (`A0_DEPOSIT_GAP_LIMIT`, recovery). The pre-check's GAP refusal
  compares the counter with `recoverA0Deposits`' result, so it follows without a code change (its two rows moved to
  101 / 100, plus a row that 21 — the M1b refusal — now proceeds). The desk's copy (`scripts/m1b-checkpoint/lib.mjs`
  `A0_GAP_LIMIT`, printed in `M1b.5`'s detail) and the README text moved to 100; the README's expected numbers are now
  102 / 101. The readout's hand-written sample keeps `depositIndicesTried: 21`: that file is the byte-for-byte contract
  of the readout test, the value is a sample nothing judges, and re-chunking it for cosmetics would change a contract
  for no check. The spec's text is listed under "Spec rev 3.4 lines". Cost of the raise: up to 80 more local
  `depositRho` calls per restore (measured in Jest: the gap rows take 0.3–0.5 s with the offline fake), no request.
- **Deviations from the brief:**
  - The brief asks for `rho_change` "against the program side's golden `rhoOut` j0 row". `golden-vectors.json`'s
    `rhoOut` j0 is the SAME value as the change golden's first vector (`nullifierIn0` 847659…, out `13d78bd0…`). The
    test compares the three change-golden vectors and, through the first, the j0 row (the first vector's public inputs

  `git show 2146368:…` from the program side's repository (read-only). One full Jest run alone took about 60 s and printed

#### Spec rev 3.4 lines (Task 5)
- §7 "Deposits" / §15 "Owner" / rev 3.3 notes (S15): the gap limit is **100** (was 20), in recovery and therefore in the
  pre-check's GAP refusal. The hazard text becomes "100 consecutive expired or front-run deposits hide every later own
  deposit". R1-m4 is decided (S15), no longer open.
- §7 "Change notes", as built: the attribution runs in sync order, one local `matchSpent(handle, [n], spentRhos)` per
  synced nullifier not yet attributed, until every spent note is attributed; a round that attributes nothing refuses
  (`E_A0_RECOVERY_NATIVE`). A spend of ours whose change leaf is not ours (another `change_d`), a `Withdraw` event without
  its instruction, or a spend above the input is counted (`unmatchedChangeLeaves`), not imported, not thrown. A zero
  change is a note (amount 0). Two withdrawals with one nullifier refuse (`E_A0_RECOVERY_DUPLICATE_NULLIFIER`) when a
  note of ours is spent.
- §7 "Accounts", as built: the destinations are those of every withdrawal that spent a note of ours. The walk also stops
  once every destination matched. A match on the main changes no role. `cli`: no walk. The registry is written before
  the notes, and an unreadable registry refuses the restore (no replace).
- §8: a recovered `spent` note that names its `spentTx` replaces a stored `spent` note (chain truth); one without
  `spentTx` does not.
- §3 "Change note" / §15: the program side's golden change-commitment vectors (2146368) confirm the equation; their

### Task 6: The native confirmation — `confirmUnshield` in Kotlin (`A0Confirm.kt`, `A0ConfirmController.kt`), its strings under the privacy guard, `a0ConfirmUnshield` / `confirmA0Unshield` in JS, and the Kotlin JVM CI job (spec §4, I10, S4, S7; controller rulings 8 and 10). What it adds:
- **the React method `confirmUnshield(handle, owner, amount, fee) -> {authId, owner, ata}`** — the ONE new method of `NocturaProverModule`. Rust `parseUnshield` parses the three strings; Kotlin renders ITS OWN dialog from Rust's answer only (the owner whole, the token account labelled "Token account", "Destination receives exactly … NOC (… base units)", "Relayer fee … NOC, taken from your shielded balance", the pool); then `BiometricPrompt` (`androidx.biometric` 1.1.0); and only on that approval, within 60 s of the request, Rust `authorizeUnshield` with the PARSED values. `parseUnshield` / `authorizeUnshield` stay `internal` and non-React; JS never holds an authorization it could forge;
- **the decision logic as a plain-Kotlin state machine** (`A0ConfirmMachine`, no Android type): one request at a time (`E_A0_CONFIRM_BUSY`); a null / finishing activity refuses with no dialog (`…_NO_ACTIVITY`); a gesture with `FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED` **or** `FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED` anywhere in it is ignored (not refused); pause / stop / destroy (a recreation) during the dialog or the prompt fails closed (`…_INTERRUPTED`); 60 s from the request (`…_TIMEOUT`, also when the approval arrives at the deadline before the timer fires); cancel, the prompt's errors (`…_CANCELLED` / `…_BIOMETRIC`); `keysClose` / a second `keysOpen` fail a waiting confirmation (`…_SESSION`); every ticket settles exactly once;
- **the window** (`A0ConfirmController` + `A0ConfirmDialog`): `FLAG_SECURE` on the dialog's window, `setHideOverlayWindows(true)` on API 31+ (manifest: `HIDE_OVERLAY_WINDOWS`, a normal permission), `filterTouchesWhenObscured` on Approve plus the gesture's flags to the machine, the activity re-checked RESUMED when the dialog is about to show, a lifecycle observer, a main-thread timer;
- **the authenticator matrix, measured on the AAR** (ruling 8): API 30+ `BIOMETRIC_STRONG | DEVICE_CREDENTIAL`; 24–29 `BIOMETRIC_STRONG`; `BIOMETRIC_WEAK` never; a device without a usable authenticator for its level refuses (`…_NO_AUTHENTICATOR`). A JVM test calls androidx's OWN `AuthenticatorUtils.isSupportedCombination` at every level 24…36;
- **the dialog's strings** in `res/values/a0_confirm_strings.xml`, read by the privacy-claims guard (with a planted-claim negative control);
- **JS:** `a0ConfirmUnshield` in `nativeProverBridge.ts` (decimal u64 strings out, the answer's shape checked: exactly `{authId: 32 lowercase hex, owner, ata}` else `E_A0_CONFIRM_RESULT`) and `confirmA0Unshield` in `src/modules/shielded/a0/unshieldConfirm.ts` (the approved owner must be the requested one and the approved `ata` must equal JS's own `a0AtaOf(owner)`, else `E_A0_CONFIRM_MISMATCH` — the abort of §4 step 4);

- **What later tasks rely on:**
  - **Task 7** calls `confirmA0Unshield(handle, {owner, amount, fee: quote.fee})` AFTER the quote, on the handle it will prove with, and passes `approval.authId` to `a0Prove(handle, 'withdraw_change', …)`; it uses `approval.owner` / `approval.ata` as the payload's `terms.owner` / `terms.ata` (Task 3's builder re-checks the ATA). Every `E_A0_CONFIRM_*` and every Rust refusal of the request is a refusal of THIS attempt: nothing was recorded (or what was recorded dies with the handle) — no note state changes, the reservation is released.
  - **Task 7 — the re-confirmation rule meets a Rust rule.** Rust holds ONE authorization at a time and refuses a second `authorizeUnshield` while one is live (`E_A0_AUTH_IN_FLIGHT`, M1a `state.rs`). That refusal comes AFTER the human approved the new dialog. So when §6.7 discards a proof-less approval (changed terms, root out of the ring) and asks for a NEW confirmation, Task 7 must first kill the old one: close the handle and open a new one (`keysClose` kills it — and with this task also fails a dialog still waiting), or let a `prove` consume it. Never confirm twice on one live approval.
  - **Task 7 — the handle and the app background.** §3 m5 closes the handle on background "unless a native confirmation is in flight". With this task the order does not matter: backgrounding pauses the activity, which fails the confirmation closed (`E_A0_CONFIRM_INTERRUPTED`), and a `keysClose` during the dialog fails it closed too (`E_A0_CONFIRM_SESSION`).
  - **Task 8** builds the screens around it (the button that starts the unshield: 500 ms debounce, disabled on tap) and the user-facing text for each `E_A0_CONFIRM_*` code; the guard's strings-resource row exists — Task 8 adds the new screen directories.
  - **Task 9** runs `A0ConfirmWindowTest` on the phone (one `am instrument -e class` line, below), records the phone's `ro.build.version.sdk` (it decides which matrix row the checkpoint proves), and lists the native dialog in the owner's visual pass (undrawn: built from platform widgets, not the design system).

**The rule, stated once.** The dialog is a control against honest-code mistakes and UI spoofing, not against a compromised JS (S7, §2). So the code is built for one property: a `withdraw_change` proof can exist only for `{owner, ata, amount, fee}` that Rust parsed, that this dialog showed in full, and that a human approved with a strong biometric or the device credential, once, within 60 s, while the app's window was in front and unobscured. Every path that is not that — another request in flight, no activity, an obscured tap, a pause, a timeout, a cancel, a closed session — ends the request with a stable refusal and records nothing. The decision logic is a plain-Kotlin machine so the JVM (and now CI) can hold every rule; what only a real window can show is an instrumented class that the phone runs.

Read: `STRONG | CREDENTIAL` (32783) is supported iff API < 28 or API > 29; `CREDENTIAL` alone (32768) iff API ≥ 30; `WEAK | CREDENTIAL` (33023) always. At API ≤ 28 with a credential allowed, androidx manages the credential button itself, and `onDeviceCredentialButtonPressed` → `launchConfirmCredentialActivity` (`KeyguardManager.createConfirmDeviceCredentialIntent`, started for a result) — a separate ACTIVITY, which pauses ours. The matrix this task pins (Notes) follows from these lines; `A0AuthenticatorsTest` then calls the library's own `isSupportedCombination` at every level (Step 2), so the pin cannot drift from the AAR. This is also the version `react-native-keychain` packages (`node_modules/react-native-keychain/android/build.gradle:76`, `implementation 'androidx.biometric:biometric:1.1.0@aar'`); 1.1.0 is the latest stable release (Google Maven lists 1.2.0-alpha05 and 1.4.0-beta01 above it).

```kotlin
package com.nocturawallet.prover

import com.nocturawallet.prover.A0ConfirmMachine.Begin
import com.nocturawallet.prover.A0ConfirmMachine.Phase
import com.nocturawallet.prover.A0ConfirmMachine.Step
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertSame
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

/**
 * The native confirmation's decision logic (spec §4 steps 3–5, I10; §14 "Kotlin (M1c)": a touch
 * delivered with FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED does not approve; a null currentActivity refuses; a
 * second request while one is in flight refuses; activity recreation during the prompt fails
 * closed) — plus the 60 s timeout, cancel, the prompt's errors, keysClose / keysOpen, and the
 * exactly-once rule. The window itself (FLAG_SECURE, the overlay hiding, the framework's touch
 * filter) is what only the phone shows: androidTest A0ConfirmWindowTest.
 */
class A0ConfirmMachineTest {
    private var clock = 1_000_000L
    private val m = A0ConfirmMachine({ clock })

    private fun started(): Long {
        val b = m.begin(activityPresent = true)
        assertTrue("$b", b is Begin.Started)
        return (b as Begin.Started).ticket
    }

    /** A request with its dialog on screen. */
    private fun inDialog(): Long {
        val t = started()
        assertSame(Step.Continue, m.shown(t))
        assertEquals(Phase.DIALOG, m.phase())
        return t
    }

    /** A request whose prompt is up. */
    private fun inPrompt(): Long {
        val t = inDialog()
        assertSame(Step.Continue, m.approve(t, 0))
        assertEquals(Phase.PROMPT, m.phase())
        return t
    }

    private fun refused(r: A0ConfirmRefusal) = Step.Refuse(r)

    // ---- §14 row 1: an obscured touch does not approve

    @Test
    fun aTouchDeliveredWhileObscuredDoesNotApprove() {
        val t = inDialog()
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.approve(t, A0Touch.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.approve(t, A0Touch.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.approve(t, A0Touch.OBSCURED or 0x100))
        // ignored, not refused: the dialog stays up and an unobscured tap still works (positive control)
        assertEquals(Phase.DIALOG, m.phase())
        assertSame(Step.Continue, m.approve(t, 0))
        assertEquals(Phase.PROMPT, m.phase())
    }

    @Test
    fun aGestureObscuredAnywhereTaintsTheClickItEndsIn() {
        val down = A0Touch.accumulate(0, A0Touch.ACTION_DOWN, 0)
        val move = A0Touch.accumulate(down, 2, A0Touch.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED) // ACTION_MOVE
        val up = A0Touch.accumulate(move, 1, 0) // ACTION_UP, clean
        val t = inDialog()
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.approve(t, up))
        // a new DOWN starts afresh: the next clean gesture approves
        val clean = A0Touch.accumulate(A0Touch.accumulate(up, A0Touch.ACTION_DOWN, 0), 1, 0)
        assertEquals(0, clean)
        assertSame(Step.Continue, m.approve(t, clean))
    }

    @Test
    fun otherMotionEventFlagsDoNotCountAsObscured() {
        // FLAG_TAINTED (0x80000000) and FLAG_IS_GENERATED_GESTURE (0x8) are not the window's cover
        assertFalse(A0Touch.obscured(0x8 or Int.MIN_VALUE))
        assertEquals(0, A0Touch.accumulate(0, A0Touch.ACTION_DOWN, 0x8 or Int.MIN_VALUE))
    }

    // ---- §14 row 2: a null currentActivity refuses

    @Test
    fun noForegroundActivityRefusesWithNoDialog() {
        assertEquals(Begin.Refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.NO_ACTIVITY), m.begin(activityPresent = false))
        assertEquals(Phase.IDLE, m.phase())
        assertNull(m.live())
        // nothing was claimed: the next request with an activity starts (control)
        assertTrue(m.begin(activityPresent = true) is Begin.Started)
    }

    // ---- §14 row 3: a second request while one is in flight refuses

    @Test
    fun aSecondRequestWhileOneIsInFlightIsRefusedAndTheFirstIsUntouched() {
        for (setup in listOf<() -> Long>({ started() }, { inDialog() }, { inPrompt() })) {
            val t = setup()
            val before = m.phase()
            assertEquals(Begin.Refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.BUSY), m.begin(true))
            assertEquals(Begin.Refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.BUSY), m.begin(false))
            assertEquals(t, m.live())
            assertEquals(before, m.phase())
            assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED), m.cancel(t))
        }
        val t = inPrompt()
        assertEquals(Begin.Refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.BUSY), m.begin(true))
        // the first still completes
        assertSame(Step.Authorize, m.promptSucceeded(t))
        assertEquals(Begin.Refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.BUSY), m.begin(true)) // AUTHORIZING is in flight too
        assertTrue(m.authorized(t))
        assertTrue(m.begin(true) is Begin.Started)
    }

    // ---- §14 row 4: recreation (pause / stop / destroy) during the dialog or the prompt fails closed

    @Test
    fun recreationDuringThePromptFailsClosedAndALateApprovalAuthorizesNothing() {
        val t = inPrompt()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.INTERRUPTED), m.interrupted(t))
        assertEquals(Phase.IDLE, m.phase())
        // the prompt's success arriving after the pause (the old fragment's callback) is ignored
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.promptSucceeded(t))
        assertFalse(m.authorized(t))
    }

    @Test
    fun recreationDuringTheDialogOrBeforeItIsShownFailsClosed() {
        val a = inDialog()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.INTERRUPTED), m.interrupted(a))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.approve(a, 0))
        val b = started()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.INTERRUPTED), m.interrupted(b))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.shown(b))
    }

    @Test
    fun aPauseAfterTheRequestEndedChangesNothing() {
        val t = inPrompt()
        assertSame(Step.Authorize, m.promptSucceeded(t))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.interrupted(t)) // AUTHORIZING: the Rust call is under way
        assertTrue(m.authorized(t))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.interrupted(t))
    }

    // ---- the 60 s timeout

    @Test
    fun noApprovalWithin60sIsATimeout() {
        val t = inDialog()
        clock += 59_999
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.timeout(t)) // early timer: not yet
        clock += 1
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT), m.timeout(t))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.approve(t, 0))
    }

    @Test
    fun anApprovalAtTheDeadlineIsATimeoutEvenBeforeTheTimerFires() {
        val t = inPrompt()
        clock += A0ConfirmMachine.TIMEOUT_MS
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT), m.promptSucceeded(t))
        assertFalse(m.authorized(t))
        val u = inDialog()
        clock += A0ConfirmMachine.TIMEOUT_MS
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT), m.approve(u, 0))
        val v = started()
        clock += A0ConfirmMachine.TIMEOUT_MS
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT), m.shown(v))
    }

    @Test
    fun theClockStartsAtBeginAndAnApprovalJustInsideIsAccepted() {
        val t = inPrompt()
        clock += A0ConfirmMachine.TIMEOUT_MS - 1
        assertSame(Step.Authorize, m.promptSucceeded(t))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.timeout(t)) // the timer that fires after the approval is stale
        assertTrue(m.authorized(t))
    }

    // ---- cancel and the prompt's errors

    @Test
    fun cancelInEveryWaitingPhaseIsARefusal() {
        val a = started()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED), m.cancel(a))
        val b = inDialog()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED), m.cancel(b))
        val c = inPrompt()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED), m.cancel(c))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.cancel(c))
    }

    @Test
    fun thePromptsErrorsAreRefusalsAndOnlyItsSuccessAuthorizes() {
        val a = inPrompt()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED), m.promptError(a, byUser = true))
        val b = inPrompt()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.BIOMETRIC), m.promptError(b, byUser = false))
        // a success outside the PROMPT phase never authorizes
        val c = inDialog()
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.promptSucceeded(c))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.promptError(c, byUser = false))
        assertEquals(Phase.DIALOG, m.phase())
    }

    // ---- keysClose / a second keysOpen

    @Test
    fun aSessionChangeFailsAWaitingConfirmationClosed() {
        for (setup in listOf<() -> Long>({ started() }, { inDialog() }, { inPrompt() })) {
            val t = setup()
            assertEquals(t to refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.SESSION), m.sessionChanged())
            assertEquals(Phase.IDLE, m.phase())
            assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.promptSucceeded(t))
        }
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.sessionChanged().second) // IDLE: nothing to fail
    }

    @Test
    fun aSessionChangeDuringTheRustCallIsLeftToRust() {
        val t = inPrompt()
        assertSame(Step.Authorize, m.promptSucceeded(t))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.sessionChanged().second)
        assertTrue(m.authorized(t))
    }

    // ---- exactly once

    @Test
    fun aSettledTicketNeverSettlesAgainAndNeverTouchesTheNextRequest() {
        val old = inPrompt()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED), m.cancel(old))
        val next = inDialog()
        for (s in listOf(
            m.shown(old), m.approve(old, 0), m.cancel(old), m.promptError(old, true), m.promptSucceeded(old),
            m.interrupted(old), m.timeout(old), m.fail(old, A0ConfirmRefusal.UI),
        )) {
            assertSame(Step.Ignore, s)
        }
        assertFalse(m.authorized(old))
        assertEquals(next, m.live())
        assertEquals(Phase.DIALOG, m.phase())
    }

    @Test
    fun authorizeIsGrantedOnceAndAuthorizedEndsItOnce() {
        val t = inPrompt()
        assertSame(Step.Authorize, m.promptSucceeded(t))
        assertSame(Step.Ignore, m.promptSucceeded(t)) // a second success callback: no second Rust call
        assertTrue(m.authorized(t))
        assertFalse(m.authorized(t))
        assertEquals(Phase.IDLE, m.phase())
    }

    @Test
    fun aSetupFailureFreesTheSlot() {
        val t = started()
        assertEquals(refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.NO_AUTHENTICATOR), m.fail(t, A0ConfirmRefusal.NO_AUTHENTICATOR))
        assertTrue(m.begin(true) is Begin.Started)
    }

    @Test
    fun everyRefusalHasAStableDistinctCode() {
        val codes = A0ConfirmRefusal.values().map { it.code }
        assertEquals(codes.size, codes.toSet().size)
        for (c in codes) assertTrue(c, c.matches(Regex("E_A0_CONFIRM_[A-Z_]+")))
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package com.nocturawallet.prover

import android.view.MotionEvent
import androidx.biometric.BiometricManager.Authenticators
import java.lang.reflect.Field
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

/**
 * The per-API-level authenticator matrix (spec §4 step 4; controller ruling 8) held against the
 * androidx.biometric 1.1.0 the app compiles with: its OWN `AuthenticatorUtils.isSupportedCombination`
 * is called for every level 24…36 with `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT` set in the unit-test android.jar —
 * so the matrix is measured on the library, not on our reading of it — plus the documented
 * matrix as a table, and the constants equal the library's and the framework's.
 */
class A0AuthenticatorsTest {
    @Test
    fun theConstantsAreTheLibrarysAndTheFrameworks() {
        assertEquals(Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG, A0Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG)
        assertEquals(Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_WEAK, A0Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_WEAK)
        assertEquals(Authenticators.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL, A0Authenticators.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL)
        assertEquals(MotionEvent.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED, A0Touch.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED)
        assertEquals(MotionEvent.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED, A0Touch.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED)
        assertEquals(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, A0Touch.ACTION_DOWN)
    }

    @Test
    fun theMatrixIsTheStatedOne() {
        val strong = A0Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG
        val strongOrCredential = A0Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG or A0Authenticators.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL
        for (sdk in 0..23) assertNull("API $sdk", A0Authenticators.forApi(sdk))
        for (sdk in 24..29) assertEquals("API $sdk", strong, A0Authenticators.forApi(sdk))
        for (sdk in 30..40) assertEquals("API $sdk", strongOrCredential, A0Authenticators.forApi(sdk))
        assertFalse(A0Authenticators.allowsCredential(strong))
        assertTrue(A0Authenticators.allowsCredential(strongOrCredential))
    }

    @Test
    fun noLevelAllowsAWeakBiometric() {
        for (sdk in 0..40) {
            val a = A0Authenticators.forApi(sdk) ?: continue
            // BIOMETRIC_WEAK (0xFF) contains BIOMETRIC_STRONG's bits; the biometric part must be exactly STRONG
            assertEquals("API $sdk", A0Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG, a and A0Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_WEAK)
        }
    }

    // ---- measured on the library

    private val sdkField: Field = Class.forName("android.os.Build\$VERSION").getDeclaredField("SDK_INT")

    // sun.misc.Unsafe by reflection (the unit-test compile classpath is android.jar, which has no sun.*):
    // SDK_INT is a static final in the android.jar stub, so it is written through Unsafe, not Field.set.
    private val unsafeClass: Class<*> = Class.forName("sun.misc.Unsafe")
    private val unsafe: Any = unsafeClass.getDeclaredField("theUnsafe").apply { isAccessible = true }.get(null)!!

    private fun setSdk(v: Int) {
        val base = unsafeClass.getMethod("staticFieldBase", Field::class.java).invoke(unsafe, sdkField)
        val offset = unsafeClass.getMethod("staticFieldOffset", Field::class.java).invoke(unsafe, sdkField) as Long
        unsafeClass.getMethod("putInt", Any::class.java, Long::class.javaPrimitiveType, Int::class.javaPrimitiveType)
            .invoke(unsafe, base, offset, v)
        check(sdkField.getInt(null) == v) { "SDK_INT could not be set to $v" }
    }

    private fun supported(sdk: Int, authenticators: Int): Boolean {
        setSdk(sdk)
        val m = Class.forName("androidx.biometric.AuthenticatorUtils")
            .getDeclaredMethod("isSupportedCombination", Int::class.javaPrimitiveType)
        m.isAccessible = true
        return m.invoke(null, authenticators) as Boolean
    }

    @Test
    fun androidxAcceptsEveryCombinationWeAskFor() {
        val saved = sdkField.getInt(null)
        try {
            for (sdk in 24..36) {
                val a = A0Authenticators.forApi(sdk)!!
                assertTrue("androidx refuses $a at API $sdk", supported(sdk, a))
            }
        } finally {
            setSdk(saved)
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun theMeasuredLibraryRefusesStrongOrCredentialOn28And29NegativeControl() {
        // the reading can fail: the combination the matrix avoids on 28–29 is refused by the library
        val saved = sdkField.getInt(null)
        val strongOrCredential = A0Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG or A0Authenticators.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL
        try {
            assertFalse(supported(28, strongOrCredential))
            assertFalse(supported(29, strongOrCredential))
            assertTrue(supported(27, strongOrCredential)) // accepted below 28 — but via a separate activity (A0Confirm.kt)
            assertTrue(supported(30, strongOrCredential))
            assertFalse(supported(29, A0Authenticators.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL)) // credential alone: 30+ only
            assertTrue(supported(30, A0Authenticators.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL))
        } finally {
            setSdk(saved)
        }
    }
}
```

Create `android/app/src/test/java/com/nocturawallet/prover/A0ConfirmTextTest.kt`:

```kotlin
package com.nocturawallet.prover

import java.io.File
import javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory
import org.json.JSONObject
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test
import org.w3c.dom.Element

/**
 * What the dialog shows (spec §4 step 3): Rust's `parseUnshield` answer read strictly, rendered
 * with the REAL format strings of `res/values/a0_confirm_strings.xml` — the full owner, the token
 * account labelled as such, "Destination receives exactly …" with the base units, the relayer fee
 * "taken from your shielded balance" (I7), the pool. Addresses and amounts come from the offline
 * ATA vectors (scripts/a0-vectors/gen-ata-vectors.mjs, web3.js) — never from the code under test.
 */
class A0ConfirmTextTest {
    private val strings: Map<String, String> = run {
        val doc = DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance().newDocumentBuilder()
            .parse(File("src/main/res/values/a0_confirm_strings.xml"))
        val nodes = doc.getElementsByTagName("string")
        (0 until nodes.length).associate { i ->
            val e = nodes.item(i) as Element
            e.getAttribute("name") to e.textContent
        }
    }
    private val vectors = JSONObject(File("../../native/noctura-prover/tests/fixtures/a0-ata-vectors.json").readText())
    private val owner = vectors.getJSONArray("owners").getJSONObject(1) // GoBAm…, an on-curve owner
    private val pool = vectors.getJSONObject("constants").getString("pool")

    private fun rust(amount: String, humanAmount: String, fee: String, humanFee: String) = JSONObject()
        .put("owner", owner.getString("owner"))
        .put("ata", owner.getString("ata"))
        .put("amount", amount)
        .put("fee", fee)
        .put("humanAmount", humanAmount)
        .put("humanFee", humanFee)
        .put("pool", pool)

    private fun render(p: A0ParsedUnshield) = A0ConfirmText.render(
        p,
        destinationLabel = strings.getValue("a0_confirm_destination_label"),
        tokenAccountLabel = strings.getValue("a0_confirm_token_account_label"),
        amountFormat = strings.getValue("a0_confirm_amount_line"),
        feeFormat = strings.getValue("a0_confirm_fee_line"),
        poolLabel = strings.getValue("a0_confirm_pool_label"),
    )

    @Test
    fun theDialogShowsRustsValuesWholeWithTheResourcesWording() {
        val amounts = vectors.getJSONArray("amounts")
        val a = amounts.getJSONObject(amounts.length() - 1)
        val f = amounts.getJSONObject(3) // 10000 → 0.00001, the live quote's minFee
        val p = A0ParsedUnshield.from(rust(a.getString("units"), a.getString("human"), f.getString("units"), f.getString("human")))
        assertNotNull(p)
        val t = render(p!!)
        assertEquals(owner.getString("owner"), t.owner) // whole, 44 characters, never cut
        assertEquals(44, t.owner.length)
        assertEquals(owner.getString("ata"), t.ata)
        assertEquals("Token account", t.tokenAccountLabel)
        assertEquals("Destination (wallet address)", t.destinationLabel)
        assertEquals(
            "Destination receives exactly ${a.getString("human")} NOC (${a.getString("units")} base units)",
            t.amountLine,
        )
        assertEquals("Relayer fee 0.00001 NOC, taken from your shielded balance", t.feeLine)
        assertEquals(pool, t.pool)
        assertEquals("Pool", t.poolLabel)
    }

    @Test
    fun theResourceHasEveryStringTheCodeNames() {
        val names = File("src/main/java/com/nocturawallet/prover/A0ConfirmController.kt").readText()
            .let { Regex("""R\.string\.(\w+)""").findAll(it).map { m -> m.groupValues[1] }.toSet() }
        assertTrue(names.size >= 9)
        for (n in names) assertTrue("missing string $n", strings.containsKey(n))
        assertEquals(names, strings.keys) // and nothing unused
    }

    @Test
    fun parseUnshieldsAnswerIsReadStrictly() {
        val good = rust("1", "0.000000001", "0", "0")
        assertNotNull(A0ParsedUnshield.from(good))
        // negative controls: a key more, a key less, a non-string, an empty string, not an object
        assertNull(A0ParsedUnshield.from(JSONObject(good.toString()).put("extra", "x")))
        assertNull(A0ParsedUnshield.from(JSONObject(good.toString()).apply { remove("pool") }))
        assertNull(A0ParsedUnshield.from(JSONObject(good.toString()).put("amount", 1)))
        assertNull(A0ParsedUnshield.from(JSONObject(good.toString()).put("ata", "")))
        assertNull(A0ParsedUnshield.from(good.toString()))
        assertNull(A0ParsedUnshield.from(null))
    }
}
```

Create `src/modules/shielded/a0/__tests__/unshieldConfirm.test.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The JS half of the native confirmation (spec §4 step 4): the approval's owner must be the one
 * asked for, and its token account must equal JS's OWN ATA(owner, mint) — else the unshield aborts.
 * Owners and ATAs come from the OFFLINE vectors (scripts/a0-vectors/gen-ata-vectors.mjs, web3.js),
 * never from the code under test; the real web3.js derives (a PDA under the app-wide mock is vacuous).
 */
import {readFileSync} from 'fs';
import {join} from 'path';

jest.mock('@solana/web3.js', () =>
  jest.requireActual<typeof import('../__testing__/realWeb3')>('../__testing__/realWeb3').loadRealWeb3(),
);

import type {A0Handle, A0UnshieldApproval} from '../../../zkProver/nativeProverBridge';
import {A0ConfirmMismatchError, confirmA0Unshield} from '../unshieldConfirm';

interface OwnerVector {
  owner: string;
  ata: string;
  verdict: string;
}
const VECTORS = JSON.parse(
  readFileSync(join(__dirname, '../../../../../native/noctura-prover/tests/fixtures/a0-ata-vectors.json'), 'utf8'),
) as {owners: OwnerVector[]};
const OK = VECTORS.owners.filter(o => o.verdict === 'ok');
const H = '7' as A0Handle;
const AUTH = '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef';

function nativeAnswering(answer: A0UnshieldApproval) {
  return jest.fn(async () => answer);
}

describe('confirmA0Unshield — the approval is held to the request (§4 step 4)', () => {
  it('reads at least five on-curve owners from the offline vectors (non-vacuous)', () => {
    expect(OK.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(5);
  });

  it.each(OK.map(o => [o.owner, o] as const))('accepts %s with its own ATA (positive control)', async (_n, o) => {
    const confirm = nativeAnswering({authId: AUTH, owner: o.owner, ata: o.ata});
    await expect(confirmA0Unshield(H, {owner: o.owner, amount: 5n, fee: 10_000n}, {confirm})).resolves.toEqual({
      authId: AUTH,
      owner: o.owner,
      ata: o.ata,
    });
    expect(confirm).toHaveBeenCalledWith(H, o.owner, 5n, 10_000n);
  });

  it('aborts when the token account is another owner’s ATA', async () => {
    const [a, b] = OK;
    const confirm = nativeAnswering({authId: AUTH, owner: a!.owner, ata: b!.ata});
    await expect(confirmA0Unshield(H, {owner: a!.owner, amount: 5n, fee: 0n}, {confirm})).rejects.toMatchObject({
      code: 'E_A0_CONFIRM_MISMATCH',
      message: 'the approved token account is not ATA(owner, mint)',
    });
  });

  it('aborts when the token account is the owner itself (a token account is never the owner)', async () => {
    const [a] = OK;
    const confirm = nativeAnswering({authId: AUTH, owner: a!.owner, ata: a!.owner});
    await expect(confirmA0Unshield(H, {owner: a!.owner, amount: 5n, fee: 0n}, {confirm})).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      A0ConfirmMismatchError,
    );
  });

  it('aborts when the approved owner is not the requested one, even with that owner’s correct ATA', async () => {
    const [a, b] = OK;
    const confirm = nativeAnswering({authId: AUTH, owner: b!.owner, ata: b!.ata});
    await expect(confirmA0Unshield(H, {owner: a!.owner, amount: 5n, fee: 0n}, {confirm})).rejects.toMatchObject({
      code: 'E_A0_CONFIRM_MISMATCH',
      message: 'the approved owner is not the requested one',
    });
  });

  it('passes a native refusal through with its code', async () => {
    const confirm = jest.fn(async () => {
      throw Object.assign(new Error('the confirmation was cancelled'), {code: 'E_A0_CONFIRM_CANCELLED'});
    });
    await expect(confirmA0Unshield(H, {owner: OK[0]!.owner, amount: 1n, fee: 0n}, {confirm})).rejects.toMatchObject({
      code: 'E_A0_CONFIRM_CANCELLED',
    });
  });
});
```

Create `scripts/android-jvm/check-reports.test.mjs`:

```js
import {test} from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import {mkdtempSync, writeFileSync, rmSync} from 'node:fs';
import {tmpdir} from 'node:os';
import {join} from 'node:path';
import {spawnSync} from 'node:child_process';
import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
import {judge, readSuites} from './check-reports.mjs';

const script = fileURLToPath(new URL('./check-reports.mjs', import.meta.url));

function reports(rows) {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'jvm-reports-'));
  for (const [name, tests, skipped = 0, failures = 0, errors = 0] of rows) {
    writeFileSync(
      join(dir, `TEST-${name}.xml`),
      `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<testsuite name="${name}" tests="${tests}" skipped="${skipped}" failures="${failures}" errors="${errors}" timestamp="2026-11-17T00:00:00" hostname="h" time="0.1">\n</testsuite>\n`,
    );
  }
  return dir;
}

const run = (dir, classes) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [script, dir, ...classes], {encoding: 'utf8'});

test('every named class ran and passed: exit 0 (positive control)', () => {
  const dir = reports([['a.B', 3], ['a.C', 1]]);
  try {
    const r = run(dir, ['a.B', 'a.C']);
    assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
    assert.match(r.stdout, /2 classes, 4 tests, all ran and passed/);
  } finally {
    rmSync(dir, {recursive: true});
  }
});

test('each defect is refused (negative controls)', () => {
  const cases = [
    [[['a.B', 3]], ['a.B', 'a.C'], /a\.C: no report/],
    [[['a.B', 0]], ['a.B'], /a\.B: 0 tests/],
    [[['a.B', 3, 1]], ['a.B'], /a\.B: 1 skipped/],
    [[['a.B', 3, 0, 1]], ['a.B'], /a\.B: 1 failures/],
    [[['a.B', 3, 0, 0, 2]], ['a.B'], /a\.B: 2 errors/],
    [[['a.B', 3], ['a.X', 1]], ['a.B'], /a\.X: a report for a class the job does not name/],
  ];
  for (const [rows, classes, why] of cases) {
    const dir = reports(rows);
    try {
      const r = run(dir, classes);
      assert.equal(r.status, 1, `${why}: ${r.stdout}`);
      assert.match(r.stderr, why);
    } finally {
      rmSync(dir, {recursive: true});
    }
  }
});

test('a report without counts is an error, never a pass', () => {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'jvm-reports-'));
  try {
    writeFileSync(join(dir, 'TEST-a.B.xml'), '<testsuite name="a.B" tests="3">');
    assert.throws(() => readSuites(dir), /has no skipped/);
    assert.notEqual(run(dir, ['a.B']).status, 0);
  } finally {
    rmSync(dir, {recursive: true});
  }
});

test('usage errors exit 2', () => {
  assert.equal(spawnSync(process.execPath, [script], {encoding: 'utf8'}).status, 2);
});

test('judge reads the counts it is given', () => {
  const suites = new Map([['a.B', {tests: 1, skipped: 0, failures: 0, errors: 0}]]);
  assert.deepEqual(judge(suites, ['a.B']), []);
});
```

Create `android/app/src/main/java/com/nocturawallet/prover/A0Confirm.kt`:

```kotlin
package com.nocturawallet.prover

import org.json.JSONObject

/**
 * The native confirmation of an unshield (spec 2026-11-08 shielded A0 M1 §4, I10, S4, S7): the
 * parts with no Android type in them, so the JVM tests hold them (A0ConfirmMachineTest,
 * A0AuthenticatorsTest, A0ConfirmTextTest). The window, the dialog and the BiometricPrompt that
 * drive them are [A0ConfirmController] and [A0ConfirmDialog].
 */

/** A refusal of `confirmUnshield`: a stable code and a fixed message (nothing from JS, nothing secret). */
internal enum class A0ConfirmRefusal(val code: String, val message: String) {
    BUSY("E_A0_CONFIRM_BUSY", "another confirmation is in flight"),
    NO_ACTIVITY("E_A0_CONFIRM_NO_ACTIVITY", "the app is not in the foreground"),
    NO_AUTHENTICATOR("E_A0_CONFIRM_NO_AUTHENTICATOR", "no strong biometric or device credential is usable on this device"),
    CANCELLED("E_A0_CONFIRM_CANCELLED", "the confirmation was cancelled"),
    TIMEOUT("E_A0_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT", "no approval within 60 s"),
    BIOMETRIC("E_A0_CONFIRM_BIOMETRIC", "the biometric prompt ended without an approval"),
    INTERRUPTED("E_A0_CONFIRM_INTERRUPTED", "the app was paused, stopped or recreated during the confirmation"),
    SESSION("E_A0_CONFIRM_SESSION", "the key session was closed or replaced during the confirmation"),
    UI("E_A0_CONFIRM_UI", "the confirmation could not be shown"),
}

/**
 * The confirmation's decision logic (§4 steps 3–5 and the window and lifecycle rules), one request
 * at a time, every method synchronized: JS calls arrive on React Native's native-modules thread,
 * the dialog and the prompt call back on the UI thread, and `keysOpen` / `keysClose` may land
 * from either side of a confirmation.
 *
 * Each request gets a ticket. Every event names its ticket and is [Step.Ignore]d unless that
 * ticket is the live one in the phase the event belongs to, so a late callback of a settled
 * request (the prompt's ERROR_CANCELED after we cancelled it, a timer that fires after an
 * approval) can never settle anything twice or touch the next request. A [Step.Refuse] returns
 * the machine to IDLE in the same step; [Step.Authorize] moves it to AUTHORIZING, from which only
 * [authorized] leaves.
 *
 * The 60 s run from [begin] on [now] (the controller passes `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime`, which
 * counts deep sleep — CLOCK_BOOTTIME, like Rust's 120 s); an approval at or past the deadline is a
 * timeout even if the timer has not fired yet.
 */
internal class A0ConfirmMachine(private val now: () -> Long, private val timeoutMs: Long = TIMEOUT_MS) {
    enum class Phase { IDLE, STARTING, DIALOG, PROMPT, AUTHORIZING }

    sealed class Begin {
        data class Started(val ticket: Long) : Begin()

        data class Refused(val refusal: A0ConfirmRefusal) : Begin()
    }

    sealed class Step {
        /** Nothing happens: a stale ticket, an event of another phase, an obscured touch. */
        object Ignore : Step()

        /** The transition happened; the caller carries on (shows the dialog's next part, the prompt). */
        object Continue : Step()

        /** The biometric approved within the deadline: call `authorizeUnshield` now, exactly once. */
        object Authorize : Step()

        /** Settle the request with this refusal; the machine is IDLE again. */
        data class Refuse(val refusal: A0ConfirmRefusal) : Step()
    }

    companion object {
        const val TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000L
    }

    private var phase = Phase.IDLE
    private var ticket = 0L
    private var deadline = 0L

    @Synchronized fun phase(): Phase = phase

    /** The live ticket, or null when IDLE. */
    @Synchronized fun live(): Long? = if (phase == Phase.IDLE) null else ticket

    /**
     * A new request. Refused, with the live one untouched, while another is in flight; refused
     * when there is no foreground activity to show a dialog in (§4: "currentActivity null →
     * refusal, no dialog").
     */
    @Synchronized fun begin(activityPresent: Boolean): Begin {
        if (phase != Phase.IDLE) return Begin.Refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.BUSY)
        if (!activityPresent) return Begin.Refused(A0ConfirmRefusal.NO_ACTIVITY)
        ticket += 1
        phase = Phase.STARTING
        deadline = now() + timeoutMs
        return Begin.Started(ticket)
    }

    private fun live(t: Long, vararg phases: Phase): Boolean = t == ticket && phase in phases

    private fun expired(): Boolean = now() >= deadline

    private fun refuse(r: A0ConfirmRefusal): Step {
        phase = Phase.IDLE
        return Step.Refuse(r)
    }

    /** The dialog is on screen. */
    @Synchronized fun shown(t: Long): Step = when {
        !live(t, Phase.STARTING) -> Step.Ignore
        expired() -> refuse(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT)
        else -> {
            phase = Phase.DIALOG
            Step.Continue
        }
    }

    /**
     * The approve control was clicked; [touchFlags] are the `MotionEvent` flags of the gesture that
     * clicked it ([A0Touch.accumulate]). A gesture with FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED or
     * FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED is ignored — not a refusal: the dialog stays up and an
     * unobscured tap still works (I10: "a touch delivered while obscured is ignored").
     */
    @Synchronized fun approve(t: Long, touchFlags: Int): Step = when {
        !live(t, Phase.DIALOG) -> Step.Ignore
        A0Touch.obscured(touchFlags) -> Step.Ignore
        expired() -> refuse(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT)
        else -> {
            phase = Phase.PROMPT
            Step.Continue
        }
    }

    /** The user cancelled (the dialog's Cancel, back). */
    @Synchronized fun cancel(t: Long): Step =
        if (live(t, Phase.STARTING, Phase.DIALOG, Phase.PROMPT)) refuse(A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED) else Step.Ignore

    /** The prompt ended with an error; [byUser] = the user cancelled it (ERROR_USER_CANCELED / NEGATIVE_BUTTON). */
    @Synchronized fun promptError(t: Long, byUser: Boolean): Step =
        if (!live(t, Phase.PROMPT)) {
            Step.Ignore
        } else {
            refuse(if (byUser) A0ConfirmRefusal.CANCELLED else A0ConfirmRefusal.BIOMETRIC)
        }

    /** The prompt approved. Only now — and only before the deadline — may Rust record an authorization. */
    @Synchronized fun promptSucceeded(t: Long): Step = when {
        !live(t, Phase.PROMPT) -> Step.Ignore
        expired() -> refuse(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT)
        else -> {
            phase = Phase.AUTHORIZING
            Step.Authorize
        }
    }

    /** `authorizeUnshield` returned (ok or refused): the request is over. True only for the live ticket. */
    @Synchronized fun authorized(t: Long): Boolean {
        if (!live(t, Phase.AUTHORIZING)) return false
        phase = Phase.IDLE
        return true
    }

    /**
     * The activity was paused, stopped or destroyed (a recreation is a pause then a destroy) while
     * the dialog or the prompt was up: fail closed, the user starts again (I10).
     */
    @Synchronized fun interrupted(t: Long): Step =
        if (live(t, Phase.STARTING, Phase.DIALOG, Phase.PROMPT)) refuse(A0ConfirmRefusal.INTERRUPTED) else Step.Ignore

    /** The 60 s timer fired. Ignored if, by [now], the deadline has not passed. */
    @Synchronized fun timeout(t: Long): Step =
        if (live(t, Phase.STARTING, Phase.DIALOG, Phase.PROMPT) && expired()) refuse(A0ConfirmRefusal.TIMEOUT) else Step.Ignore

    /** A setup step failed before the prompt could approve (no authenticator, a dialog that would not show). */
    @Synchronized fun fail(t: Long, r: A0ConfirmRefusal): Step =
        if (live(t, Phase.STARTING, Phase.DIALOG, Phase.PROMPT)) refuse(r) else Step.Ignore

    /**
     * `keysClose` or a second `keysOpen` (§4: "invalidates a live authId"; §3 m5): a confirmation
     * still waiting for the human fails closed, and the caller settles the returned ticket. In
     * AUTHORIZING the call into Rust is already under way on the UI thread: Rust's one mutex
     * orders it against the close, and either order leaves no live authorization (the close kills
     * a recorded one; a stale handle is refused) — so the machine does not interfere.
     */
    @Synchronized fun sessionChanged(): Pair<Long, Step> =
        if (phase == Phase.STARTING || phase == Phase.DIALOG || phase == Phase.PROMPT) {
            ticket to refuse(A0ConfirmRefusal.SESSION)
        } else {
            ticket to Step.Ignore
        }
}

/** The obscured-window flags of a touch gesture (I10). */
internal object A0Touch {
    /** `MotionEvent.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED` (API 9). */
    const val FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED = 0x1

    /** `MotionEvent.FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED` (API 29; never set below it). */
    const val FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED = 0x2

    const val OBSCURED = FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED or FLAG_WINDOW_IS_PARTIALLY_OBSCURED

    /** `MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN`. */
    const val ACTION_DOWN = 0

    fun obscured(flags: Int): Boolean = flags and OBSCURED != 0

    /**
     * The obscured bits of every event of one gesture: a DOWN starts afresh, every later event
     * adds its bits, so one obscured event anywhere in the gesture taints the click it ends in.
     */
    fun accumulate(previous: Int, actionMasked: Int, flags: Int): Int =
        if (actionMasked == ACTION_DOWN) flags and OBSCURED else previous or (flags and OBSCURED)
}

/**
 * The authenticators the prompt allows, per API level (§4 step 4; controller ruling 8: "STRONG |
 * DEVICE_CREDENTIAL where supported, a stated fallback per API level, a level with no safe
 * combination refuses"). Measured on androidx.biometric 1.1.0 (the AAR the app resolves, sha256
 * 270c7b7d…; `AuthenticatorUtils.isSupportedCombination` and `BiometricFragment`, read with javap —
 * Task 6 Notes):
 *
 * | API      | allowed                          | why                                                          |
 * |----------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
 * | 30+      | BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL | supported; the framework prompt shows the credential itself |
 * | 28–29    | BIOMETRIC_STRONG                 | STRONG or CREDENTIAL is unsupported here; WEAK or CREDENTIAL would admit a Class 2 biometric |
 * | 24–27    | BIOMETRIC_STRONG                 | STRONG or CREDENTIAL is accepted, but androidx then launches the KeyguardManager credential ACTIVITY, which pauses ours — the lifecycle rule fails it closed every time |
 * | < 24     | none (refuse)                    | below minSdk                                                 |
 *
 * BIOMETRIC_WEAK is never allowed. A device whose level allows only BIOMETRIC_STRONG and that has
 * no strong biometric enrolled is refused (`canAuthenticate` ≠ SUCCESS → E_A0_CONFIRM_NO_AUTHENTICATOR).
 */
internal object A0Authenticators {
    /** `BiometricManager.Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG` (0x000F) — held equal by A0AuthenticatorsTest. */
    const val BIOMETRIC_STRONG = 0x000F

    /** `BiometricManager.Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_WEAK` (0x00FF) — never used; named for the tests. */
    const val BIOMETRIC_WEAK = 0x00FF

    /** `BiometricManager.Authenticators.DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` (0x8000). */
    const val DEVICE_CREDENTIAL = 0x8000

    const val MIN_SDK = 24

    fun forApi(sdk: Int): Int? = when {
        sdk < MIN_SDK -> null
        sdk >= 30 -> BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL
        else -> BIOMETRIC_STRONG
    }

    /** With a device credential allowed the prompt has no negative button (androidx requires it absent). */
    fun allowsCredential(authenticators: Int): Boolean = authenticators and DEVICE_CREDENTIAL != 0
}

/**
 * Rust's `parseUnshield` answer (§3: `{owner, ata, amount, fee, humanAmount, humanFee, pool}`,
 * every value computed in Rust; amounts as decimal strings). The dialog shows these and nothing
 * else; `authorizeUnshield` is called with [owner], [amount], [fee] from here — the values the
 * human saw — never with the strings JS passed.
 */
internal data class A0ParsedUnshield(
    val owner: String,
    val ata: String,
    val amount: String,
    val fee: String,
    val humanAmount: String,
    val humanFee: String,
    val pool: String,
) {
    companion object {
        private val KEYS = listOf("owner", "ata", "amount", "fee", "humanAmount", "humanFee", "pool")

        /** Exactly the seven keys, each a non-empty string; anything else is null (E_A0_INTERNAL). */
        fun from(value: Any?): A0ParsedUnshield? {
            if (value !is JSONObject) return null
            if (value.length() != KEYS.size) return null
            val v = KEYS.map { k -> (value.opt(k) as? String)?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() } ?: return null }
            return A0ParsedUnshield(v[0], v[1], v[2], v[3], v[4], v[5], v[6])
        }
    }
}

/**
 * The dialog's text (§4 step 3), from the format strings of `res/values/a0_confirm_strings.xml`
 * (passed in, so the JVM test renders the real resource). The owner and the token account are
 * whole — never truncated, never ellipsized (substitution attacks live in matching prefixes).
 */
internal data class A0ConfirmText(
    val destinationLabel: String,
    val owner: String,
    val tokenAccountLabel: String,
    val ata: String,
    val amountLine: String,
    val feeLine: String,
    val poolLabel: String,
    val pool: String,
) {
    companion object {
        fun render(
            p: A0ParsedUnshield,
            destinationLabel: String,
            tokenAccountLabel: String,
            amountFormat: String,
            feeFormat: String,
            poolLabel: String,
        ): A0ConfirmText = A0ConfirmText(
            destinationLabel = destinationLabel,
            owner = p.owner,
            tokenAccountLabel = tokenAccountLabel,
            ata = p.ata,
            amountLine = String.format(java.util.Locale.ROOT, amountFormat, p.humanAmount, p.amount),
            feeLine = String.format(java.util.Locale.ROOT, feeFormat, p.humanFee),
            poolLabel = poolLabel,
            pool = p.pool,
        )
    }
}
```
